```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(tictoc)
library(tidylog)

# load package managed by The Marmot Project to export data to .csv for accessibility
library(ybamaRmot)
# load and export blood smear data
blood_raw <- ybamaRmot::tb_bloodcount |>
  subset(useful_smear == "1")
write_csv(blood_raw, "blood_raw.csv")
# load and export all social data on allogrooming 
allogroom_raw <- ybamaRmot::tb_socint |>
  subset(interac_type == "allogroom")
write_csv(allogroom_raw, "allogroom_raw.csv")

```

## My question

*Route*: My own, using data from The Marmot Project [@ybamaRmot]

*Question*: Is allogrooming associated with immune health in a facultatively social mammal?

*Background and Prediction*: Allogrooming is an affiliative social behavior where animals clean one another to facilitate social bonding [@RAULT2019113]. In multiple rodent species, distressed animals exhibit fewer anxiety-like behaviors after receiving allogrooming [@LIM2023105391]. In primates, receiving grooming has shown to reduce stress through lowering heart rate and releasing opioids in the blood, and decreasing stress related behaviors [@YATES2022104740]. Low levels of maternal licking and grooming alter the stress-response of their offspring, leading to heightened stress reactivity and more anxious or fearful behavior in adulthood [@PETELLE201786]. Quantification of leukocyte profiles is a common measure of immunocompetence. Lymphocytes and neutrophils are the two most abundant types of white blood cells found in the immune system of mammals. Neutrophils increase and/or lymphocytes decrease in response to chronic stress through the elevation of glucocorticoids (GCs) [@MARTIN200970]. Because of this, neutrophil to lymphocyte ratios (NLR) often serves as a marker of chronic stress due to the delay between exposure of a stressor and the blood cell response. I hypothesize there will be a negative relationship between allogrooming and neutrophil to lymphocyte ratios (NLR), where individuals with a lower NLR give and receive allogrooming more than individuals with a high NLR. Alternatively, this relationship may nonlinear, as allogrooming could function as a self-soothing behavior, meaning there is a chance individuals engaging in this behavior more are using it as a coping mechanism from undergoing more stressful situations, so individuals who give and receive more allogrooming have a higher NLR.

# load datasets 
blood_raw <- read_csv("data/blood_raw.csv")
allogroom_raw <- read_csv("data/allogroom_raw.csv")

# clean blood dataset and calculate NLR
blood_cleaned <- blood_raw |>
  subset(useful_smear = 1) |>
  separate_wider_delim(  # separate date, time, and uid into three columns
    cols = date_time_uid,
    delim = ".",
    names = c("date", "time", "uid") 
  ) |>
  mutate(date = lubridate::mdy(date), # change to date
         year = lubridate::year(date)) |> #add year column
  mutate(NLR = neutrophils/lymphocytes) |> #calculate NLR
  select(year, date, uid, neutrophils, lymphocytes, trypanosomes, NLR)

# clean allogroom dataset and calculate total allogrooms
